overview: This file concerns restrictions and conditions governing alien labor and employment in Japanese-ruled Taiwan (Formosa). Its principal document is a November 1932 consular report stating that Taiwan had no laws restricting aliens’ employment, although the entry of Chinese laborers was controlled through licenses issued under the Government General’s “Regulations Governing Control of Chinese Laborers.” The file also contains cross-reference sheets directing researchers to the original despatch and to a November 1934 Tokyo despatch about labor conditions and rules for the temporary admission and residence of foreign musicians, artists, actors, choristers, and other workers.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Ketcham despatch no. 925
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to despatch no. 925 concerning alien employment restrictions in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet records a despatch sent by Ketcham from Taihoku on November 15, 1932. It identifies the subject as alien employment restrictions in Taiwan, notes that a copy of the despatch is attached, and directs readers to file 800.504/36 for the original despatch.

subfiles.title: Report on alien employment restrictions in Taiwan
subfiles.from: John H. Ketcham, U.S. Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: The report explains that Taiwan imposed no restrictions on aliens’ employment but regulated the immigration of Chinese laborers.
subfiles.summary: Prepared on November 15 and mailed on November 16, 1932, the report responds to a Department of State instruction and a letter from the Secretary of Labor. It states that no Taiwanese laws, ordinances, or regulations restricted the employment of aliens. Chinese laborers, however, could enter Taiwan only after receiving licenses from immigration agents appointed by the Taiwan Government General; once lawfully admitted, they faced no employment restriction. The report cites the secretary-translator and Law Department of the Taiwan Government General as information sources and notes distribution to the Department of State and the Consulate General at Tokyo.
keywords: Regulations Governing Control of Chinese Laborers

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Garrels despatch no. 943
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a Tokyo despatch on Formosan labor conditions and the admission of foreign performers and other aliens for employment.
subfiles.summary: This sheet directs researchers to file 894A.55/4 for despatch no. 943, sent from Tokyo by Garrels on November 17, 1934. The despatch concerned labor conditions in Formosa and the conditions governing the temporary admission and residence of foreign instrumentalists, musicians, artists, actors, choristers, and other aliens seeking employment. It reportedly enclosed a copy of the relevant rules and regulations, which are not present in this file.

interest: The file provides a concise contemporary distinction between immigration control and employment regulation in colonial Taiwan: Chinese laborers were subject to licensed entry, but aliens already lawfully present were reportedly free of employment restrictions. This makes the 1932 report useful for studying Japanese colonial labor policy, Chinese mobility, and American consular information-gathering. The 1934 cross-reference broadens the subject to itinerant cultural workers and highlights how related evidence was dispersed across the State Department’s decimal filing system.
